question: What is the SI unit of mass and weight of a body, respectively?
solution:
The correct answer is __**kg, N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mass** is a fundamental property of matter that quantifies the amount of substance in an object, and its SI unit is the **kilogram (kg)**.
 
• **Weight** is the force exerted on a body due to gravity, and its SI unit is the **Newton (N)**.
 
• Weight is calculated as the product of mass and gravitational acceleration (W = mg), where g is approximately 9.81 m/s² on Earth.
 
• The kilogram (kg) is the base unit of mass in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• The Newton (N) is derived from the SI units as 1 N = 1 kg·m/s².

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mass vs Weight**:

 
 
• Mass is a scalar quantity and does not change with location, while weight is a vector quantity and changes with the gravitational field strength.
 
• Mass is measured using a balance, while weight is measured using a spring scale.
 
 
 
• **SI Units**:
 
 
• The International System of Units (SI) is the modern form of the metric system and the most widely used system of measurement.
 
• It includes seven base units: meter (m), kilogram (kg), second (s), ampere (A), kelvin (K), mole (mol), and candela (cd).
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Acceleration**:
 
 
• Gravitational acceleration (g) varies slightly over the surface of the Earth, generally taken as 9.81 m/s².
 
• Weight varies slightly depending on altitude and latitude due to variations in gravitational acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**:
 
 
• The kilogram was originally defined in 1795 as the mass of one liter of water.
 
• In 2019, the definition of the kilogram was redefined based on the Planck constant, making it more stable and accurate.
